title: Ed Fox feud; Budd and Eckstine reorganize Earl Hines's band
summary: Budd tells Hines to rebuild the band while Fox's clique left, with himself as musical director and deposits locked in the Ritz Hotel safe.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: We were talking about the band, the Earl Hines band (unintelligible). Who was on bass?
Quinn Wilson was on bass. So you know as I told you, Earl and Ed Fox was having a feud at that time so --

Yeah. Ed Fox was the manager of the Grand Terrace Hotel and he also had Earl under personal contract. And where he had power of attorney also, and so when we got back into Chicago, you know, as I told you, we had cliques in that band.
Yeah, that's what we talked about.

Walter Fuller took over his part of the clique and went in the Grand Terrace, so that left Earl, Billy Ekstein, George Dixon and myself out. So I told Earl then, I said Earl, let me tell you one thing. You went around here worrying and going on, and Earl with Baby Bell was letting him have 10 or $15.00, you know --
Baby Bell was one of the old great attempts of all time. But he loved musicians, and he used to

let Earl have money to sustain himself. And so I said, Earl, Ed Fox was billing Earl Hines, he wasn't billing Ed Fox. I said you have the name, all we got to do man is to start to sending out wires and writing letters to all of those people you've played for, and you get those deposits in. I says I'll whip the band, me and Billy Eckstein will whip the band back together for you, and hell, we can go on and play. So he says, yeah, you could do that, I says, sure. So Billy Eckstein and myself set out to get this band, in the mean time I made Willie Randall --

: Yeah, he's an alto saxophone player in the band. He became business manager and we always called LeRoy Harris -- another saxophone player that I used to -- he used to sing in the band, we called him Mr. Safe. So he was the treasurer.

And I was the musical director, so Earl -- we started to writing letters, in the meantime Willie was writing a letter to these people about Earl, and we started to book the band, and we would ask for a deposit. And we would take that deposit and put it in the safe at the Ritz Hotel. Now Earl couldn't get his hands on a bit.
